newsitem.title: USA: Thumbnail sketches of new Simpson jury.
newsitem.headline: Thumbnail sketches of new Simpson jury.

text.p: The following is a sketch of the jury chosen Friday in the O.J. Simpson civil trial. Their names have been kept confidential and they are known only by their juror numbers:

-- Juror #199: a postal worker born in Jamaica who in his 20s. He is of mixed Asian and black descent and has a college degree. He said during jury selection he was surprised at the quick verdict in the criminal case but said he had no opinion on Simpson's guilt or innocence.
-- Juror #341: a white woman who appears to be about 70. She wrote on her jury questionnaire that, in her opinion, the use of force in a relationship often predisposes a person to violence.

-- Juror #186 (new juror): a white man in his early 30s. He believes that some, but not all, police officers are corrupt. "It's wrong to assume all cops are good," he said, "but I don't say all cops are bad, either." The man also said he developed a passing interest in DNA science after watching the movie "Jurassic Park."

-- Juror #78: a woman of mixed white and Hispanic descent in her 20s. She said it would not be difficult for her to listen to arguments that police planted evidence, saying "I believe there could be dishonest people in any profession."

-- Juror #266: a white woman in her 30s who grew up in the South. She works as a stage manager for a non-profit community theatre. She said she had no preconceived notions about Simpson's guilt or innocence and knew a little about DNA -- a cornerstone of the case -- from high school biology classes.

-- Juror #257: a Hispanic woman in her 30s. She indicated on her jury questionnaire she did not pay much attention to Simpson's criminal trial -- in which he was acquitted of double murder -- and had few opinions about the case.

-- Juror #333: a black woman in her 60s. She told lawyers she felt sympathy for Fred Goldman, father of murder victim Ronald Goldman, because "it's a parent's worst nightmare to have your child die before you do." She also said: "Celebrities are human beings, just as likely to kill as any other person."
-- Juror #290: a man in his 40s believed to be of Middle Eastern descent. A company manager who specialises in arbitration, he said he would "go in with an open mind."

-- Juror #326 (new juror): a white man in his 50s who believes police are sometimes involved in cover-ups. "Of course they cover up for each other," he said."It's been done before." He also said it was "possible" that evidence in the case had been tampered with and was doubtful about blood found on a gate at Nicole Brown Simpson's home two months after the murders.

-- Juror #400 (new juror): a white woman in her 60s who said on a jury questionnaire that interracial marriages were "hard on the children." She also has strong religious beliefs but told attorneys she's "not a fanatic."
-- Juror #88: a white woman in her 30s. Asked if she would listen to arguments about evidence-planting by police, she said, "I believe anything is possible."

-- Juror #227: a white man in his 50s or 60s. He said he first thought Simpson was innocent but later decided he was "probably guilty." The man, who said his father had been a police officer, called interracial marriages "impractical."
